observations: This profile combines two mechanically INDEPENDENT locale-selection UIs (portal edit-context selector and storefront buyer-facing switcher) into one feature profile because they share the same underlying locale list (shop-locales, KB-003) and the same object (Translation) — not because they share implementation or user goal. Each is documented as a distinct capability below with its own actor/entry point; do not assume changing one affects the other. feature-profile-builder judged this coherent enough for one profile (bootstrap-request explicitly scoped both as 'switcher' concepts of the same object); reviewer may split into 2 profiles if this coupling proves confusing downstream.
unknowns: Whether GET /api/instances/{instanceId}/shop-locales is a live Shopify Admin API pass-through or a teeinblue-cached copy of it.
Whether the portal itself has any separate 'portal display language' setting elsewhere in the app (only the 2 translation pages were checked; user profile/account settings were not).
Behavior when a store has more than 2 published locales (this store only has en/vi) — untested for either switcher.
Mobile-viewport interaction behavior for the storefront switcher (only inventoried in DOM, not clicked, at mobile viewport size).

feature_profiles.name: Language/locale selection mechanisms across Translation surfaces
feature_profiles.user_goal: As a merchant editing translations, choose which of the store's published languages I am currently entering/viewing translated text for, without changing the portal's own display language. As a buyer, choose which published language I browse the storefront in (a native Shopify Markets/locale mechanism, not a teeinblue-built widget), which in turn determines which locale's Product Page Content / Dynamic Translations content I would see.

actors.permission_observed: user_id=266 successfully switched the edit-context locale on both /product-page-content and /artwork-translations without any additional auth/permission gate beyond the normal portal session.
Unauthenticated buyer successfully switched storefront locale via the header switcher with no login required (public Shopify /localization endpoint).

entry_points.path: 'Languages from <store>' combobox, identical component at the top of both /product-page-content and /artwork-translations (portal)
Header 'Language' localization-form (desktop, mobile, and footer instances) on any storefront page (Shopify Dawn theme's stock <localization-form> component)
entry_points.precondition: buyer viewing any storefront page; store has >=2 published Shopify locales

capabilities.name: Portal: locale list sourced from Shopify shop-locales
capabilities.description: Both translation pages populate their 'Languages from <store>' combobox from GET /api/instances/{instanceId}/shop-locales, which returned exactly 2 entries (en=primary, vi=non-primary), both marked published:true. The same locale count/codes were independently observed on the storefront switcher, indicating both surfaces draw from the same underlying Shopify locale publish state (mechanism-level link unconfirmed, count/code match confirmed).

capabilities.name: Portal: edit-context locale selector, does not change portal UI language
capabilities.description: Selecting a non-default locale in the combobox changes ONLY which locale's translation values are shown/edited in the form (e.g. Form header field switches to show the vi override, if any). It does NOT change the portal's own UI language — sidebar menu items, page heading, and Save/Reset button labels remain in English regardless of the selected editing locale. Confirmed identically on both /product-page-content and /artwork-translations.

capabilities.name: Storefront: header switcher is Shopify's native Markets/locale mechanism, not a teeinblue widget
capabilities.description: The header language switcher is Shopify Dawn theme's own <localization-form> component (4 instances: desktop/mobile header, desktop/mobile footer) — confirmed NOT a teeinblue-built toggle. Selecting a language submits a multipart POST https://<shop>.myshopify.com/localization (form_type=localization, _method=put, locale_code=<code>) directly to Shopify; server responds 302, redirecting to the same path with the new locale prefixed (e.g. /vi/...). This directly answers the initial business-context question: the storefront language mechanism IS Shopify's own market/locale system.

capabilities.name: Storefront: locale carried via URL path prefix, consistent across pages
capabilities.description: After switching, the locale is carried as a URL path prefix (e.g. /vi, /vi/products/...) — not a query param or purely client-side cookie toggle. Confirmed consistent between the storefront home page and the campaign 2595 product page in the same session.

state_transitions.from: portal: locale=English selected in edit-context combobox
state_transitions.to: portal: locale=Vietnamese selected in edit-context combobox
state_transitions.trigger: owner selects 'Vietnamese' from the 'Languages from <store>' combobox
state_transitions.condition: no network request triggered by the selection itself (client-side state change only); portal UI language is unaffected

state_transitions.trigger: buyer clicks 'Tiếng việt' in the header localization-form
state_transitions.condition: POST /localization returns 302, browser follows redirect to the locale-prefixed URL

observed_behavior: Portal combobox's display label capitalization ('Vietnamese') differs from the storefront switcher's own localized label ('Tiếng việt') — expected, since these are two independently-implemented pieces of UI text, not a shared component.

Country/region (market) selector sits alongside the storefront Language switcher on the same localization-form component but is a separate control — switching Language in this run did not change Country/region (observed staying 'United States').
permissions: Neither switcher required any permission check beyond the ambient session (owner session for portal, none/GUEST for storefront) in this run. No PERMISSION/cross-tenant test performed.

storefront: Header/footer 'Language' localization-form (desktop + mobile), Dawn theme, on any storefront page
api: POST https://<shop>.myshopify.com/localization (APIOP-005) — Shopify-owned, outside teeinblue's backend; feeds the storefront switcher

dependencies: product-page-content-translation profile depends on this profile's portal edit-context selector to determine save target locale, and (indirectly, via buyer's chosen locale) on the storefront switcher to determine which override a buyer sees.
dynamic-translations profile depends on this profile's portal edit-context selector to determine save/delete target locale.
risks: The portal combobox and storefront switcher are independently implemented and NOT confirmed to be driven by the exact same backend locale source (portal: possibly-cached shop-locales; storefront: Shopify's own Markets config directly) — if they ever diverge (e.g. a locale published in one system but not synced to the other), the portal could offer editing a locale buyers can never select, or vice versa. Unverified in this run (store only has 2 locales, both consistent).

unknown_areas.question: Is GET /api/instances/{instanceId}/shop-locales a live pass-through of Shopify's locale API, or a teeinblue-side cache?
unknown_areas.why_it_matters: If cached, the portal combobox could show a stale locale list after a merchant changes published locales directly in Shopify Admin, causing a mismatch between what merchants can edit and what buyers can select.

unknown_areas.question: How do both switchers behave when a store has more than 2 published locales?
unknown_areas.why_it_matters: Only a 2-option case was tested; UI patterns like scrolling comboboxes, search-within-list, or per-locale completeness indicators are unverified and could reveal layout/usability issues at scale.

unknown_areas.question: Does the storefront switcher behave the same on mobile viewport as desktop?
unknown_areas.why_it_matters: Only the mobile DOM element was inventoried, not interacted with — mobile-specific interaction bugs (e.g. touch target size, disclosure widget behavior) are unverified.

profile_relationships.note: Both switcher halves feed into which locale is edited (portal) or seen (storefront) for this feature.
Portal edit-context selector determines save/delete target locale for Dynamic Translations.
